To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the discovery of a new class of potent DPP-4 inhibitors, which is based on the use of an anti-Substitued -methylphenylalaninamide moiety, has led to the identification of a compound that is among the most potent inhibitors reported to date lacking a electrophilic trapping group.

the anti-Substituents in the P1 and P2 positions of the dipeptidic DPP-IV substrates are important for potency, that the P1 position can tolerate a variety of anti-Substituent, but that the P2 position is more restricted and that the most potent compounds lack the electrophilic traps that were present in the previously reported compounds.
(1) The phenylalanine derived DPP-IV amide inhibitors are potent and selective inhibitors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of potent and selective DPP-IV, DPP8 and/or DPP9 inhibitors.
the design and synthesis of novel DPP-IV enzyme inhibitors.
the discovery of potent and selective DPP-IV enzyme inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 1,2,5-oxadiazolyl-2-phenylalanine based inhibitors represent the most potent and selective inhibitors of DPP-IV described to date.
the 2,5-diketopiperazine scaffold is the best for DPP-IV inhibition and 1,3,4-oxazol-5-one and 1,5-dioxopyrrol-2-one are the next best.
the phenylalanine-derived DPP-IV inhibitory scaffold represents a novel class of DPP-IV modulators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anti-substituted beta-methyphenylalanine based amides have been found to be potent DDP-IV inhibitors exhibiting good selectivity over both DP8 and DDP9.
the anti-substituted beta-methyphenylalanine based DPP-IV amide inhibitors have the potential to become a lead series for the development of a DPP-IV drug.
the anti-substituted phenylalanine derived inhibitors are potent and selective inhibitors of DPP-IV, which are among the best inhibitors of this enzyme lacking an electrophile.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anti-substituted beta-methylene phenylalanine amides can serve as a new scaffold for the discovery of DPP-IV selective inhibitors.
the anti-substituted phenylalanine amide core is a promising starting point to develop potent DPP-4 inhibitors.
a phenylalanine-based amide scaffold is a viable alternative to the previously reported electrophilic-trap containing inhibitors.
